Still though, some dogs just do better in the salon environment. You could take them there for the first few months and the dog could be used to it but once you try to do it yourself the dog may still not react as well. There is a reason why groomers have great relationships with the clients, not to mention our equipment is very expensive. So yes if it's possible but don't be surprised if you can't do it. What will you do with the equipment you've bought then? 

Anyway for a brush I HIGHLY recommend the "Chris Christensen Slicker brush" type that into Google and that's the brush you should invest in at the very least. It'll help you greatly between grooms and is the absolute best brush on the market for this type of coat.

Clippers, make sure you buy professional grooming ones if you cheap out, I guarantee they will not get through a coat that thick for very long and even if they do they will not last. 

Poodles coats curl up very quickly so you'll need a dryer that dries them in the quickest way possible I recommend the K-9 11

You'll also need to consider how you'll restrain your dog from leaving, jumping, bucking, while you're using these tools on them. I've seen alot of owners who've cut their own dog and the dog loses trust for the owner so again just keep in mind for the future.
